## Motivation

-   Machine failures are rare but costly
-   Predictive maintenance enables early intervention
-   This is an anomaly detection problem
-   Which operational and sensor features are most strongly associated with machine failures?
-   Can machine failures be reliably predicted despite severe class imbalance?

## Data Overview

-   AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset (UCI ML Repository)
-   10,000 simulated industrial observations
-   Mix of numeric sensor readings and categorical machine information
-   Binary target: Machine failure
-   Failure rate ≈ 3–4%

## Key Challenges

-   Severe class imbalance (\~28:1)
-   Accuracy is misleading
-   Focus on F1 and PR-AUC instead

![](images/fail_out-2.png)

## Methods

**Baseline models** - Logistic Regression - KNN - Decision Tree - SVM

**Ensemble methods** - Random Forest - Gradient Boosting - XGBoost

## Handling Imbalance

-   Removed leakage features
-   Used class-weighting in XGBoost
-   Tuned decision threshold for F1

## Model Comparison

-   Ensemble methods outperform baselines
-   XGBoost performs best overall

![](images/output_plot.png)

## XGBoost Results

-   Hyperparameter tuning via GridSearch
-   Threshold tuning further improved F1
-   Best balance of precision and recall

## Final Performance

-   F1 ≈ 0.78
-   ROC-AUC ≈ 0.97
-   PR-AUC ≈ 0.81

![](images/best_matrix.png)

## Conclusion

-   Feature importance highlights torque, tool wear, and rotational speed
-   Final model is suitable as an early-warning system
-   Ensemble methods are effective for rare-event prediction
-   XGBoost + imbalance handling was the winning approach ![](images/features.png){width="500" height="300"}
